$295 billion. One goal. Total AI sovereignty.

China just unveiled a five-year plan to build an entirely self-sufficient national AI infrastructure. Two trillion yuan invested. Datacenters connected across the country. 80% of the technology built by Chinese companies. And Huawei Ascend chips replacing NVIDIA at every layer.

This is not an incremental policy. This is the deliberate construction of a parallel AI economy — one that does not depend on a single Western chip, framework, or cloud provider.

For global business leaders, the implications are immediate. If your AI workloads touch Chinese markets, Chinese partners, or Chinese data, they will increasingly run on infrastructure you did not build and may not fully understand. Interoperability between these two ecosystems is uncertain at best.

The companies that recognize this shift early and build dual-stack AI strategies will have a structural advantage. The ones that assume a single global compute supply chain will be caught in the middle.
